banter.headline: My captain's entire T20 career came down to one ball
banter.body: Babar Azam, my captain, walked back to the pavilion after facing ONE ball. He scored 0. I had a whole strategy for his first 10 overs. Now Rizwan has to carry the dream before my cold warms up.
banter.shareText: My captain got a duck off ball 1. I had a 50-point plan for his first over. I am now sitting with cold chai and zero hope. Rizwan please be the man today. #CricketHeartbreak

slides.headline: Unbelievable 21 runs in over 12!
slides.body: Axar Patel exploded for 21 runs in over 12, the highest of the match so far. That 21‑run over spiked the score and kept India’s bowlers on their toes.

slides.headline: Key wickets fell, Pakistan’s chances slipped.
slides.body: Babar was out lbw to Arshdeep in the very first ball. Then Rizwan was caught by Bhuvneshwar at 3.6. Later Shadab fell to a catch by Suryakumar at 13.2. Each dismissal dropped Pakistan’s win‑chance.

slides.headline: Shan Masood lights up the innings.
slides.body: Masood has accumulated 36 runs off 31 balls, the biggest partnership for Pakistan so far. His quick scoring keeps the run rate high and puts India under pressure.

slides.headline: What to look out for next 5 overs.
slides.body: Pakistan are 106/5 after 15 overs with 30 balls left. They need to keep the run rate at 7.07. The next five overs will be crucial – can the batsmen maintain the pace or will India’s bowlers tighten up?

slides.headline: Axar Patel's explosive over 12: 21 runs
slides.body: Over 12 Pakistan’s bowler Axar Patel gave away a massive 21 runs in just six balls – almost three standard deviations above the norm. No wicket fell, but the flood of boundaries changed the flow of the game.

slides.headline: Back‑to‑back wickets in over 14 swing momentum
slides.body: Hardik Pandya struck twice in over 14, taking two wickets while conceding only two runs. Those quick dismissals turned a low‑scoring over into a big turning point for Pakistan.

slides.headline: Key wicket at 13.2 drops India’s win chance
slides.body: At ball 13.2 Hardik got Shadab out (caught). India’s win probability slid from 56% to 49%, showing how a single dismissal can shift the match outlook.

slides.headline: India needs 160 in 20 overs – what to watch
slides.body: India now starts its chase: 160 runs required from 20 overs (8 runs per over). Watch the openers’ start, any early wickets, and how the powerplay is used to build momentum.

slides.headline: Early wobble: five dot balls at the start
slides.body: The innings opened with a five‑ball run‑less spell (balls 0.1‑0.5). Pakistan struggled to get going, setting a quiet tone before the first wicket fell.

slides.headline: Babar’s early dismissal shakes Pakistan
slides.body: At 1.1, Arshdeep bowled Babar to lbw. The wicket dropped Pakistan’s win chance from 45% to 36%, putting early pressure on the batting side.

slides.headline: Masood’s four sparks a small surge
slides.body: In over 3, Shan Masood struck a boundary at 3.1, lifting the win probability from 37% to 40%. The partnership with Iftikhar Ahmed added momentum.

slides.headline: What to watch in the next overs
slides.body: Keep an eye on the new partnership between Masood (19) and Iftikhar (7). Watch how Arshdeep’s next spell goes and whether Pakistan can keep a run rate above 5.5 to stay in the game.

slides.headline: Rahul gets bowled off Naseem - India's win chances drop
slides.body: At 1.5 of the innings, Rahul was bowled by Naseem Shah. India's chance to win fell from 46% to 32%.

slides.headline: Unbelievable 20‑run over from Mohammad Nawaz
slides.body: Over 12 was a fireworks display by Mohammad Nawaz who hit 20 runs in just 9 balls – the biggest over of the match. India now sits at 90/4.

slides.headline: Rohit’s wicket swings the game
slides.body: At 3.2, Haris Rauf caught Rohit with Iftikhar’s help, dropping win chances from 30% to 19%.

slides.headline: Now India needs 70 runs in 36 balls – a 11.7 RPR
slides.body: Only 16% chance to win. You need 70 runs off 36 balls – that’s a required run rate of 11.7 (runs per over). Keep bowlers tight and aim for quick boundaries.

slides.headline: Mohammad Nawaz turns the tables with 20 runs in over 12
slides.body: Nawaz unleashed a blistering over, scoring 20 runs in 6 balls, the biggest over in this innings. It jolted India’s chase, giving Pakistan a big boost in win chances.

slides.headline: Key wickets fell for India: Rahul, Rohit, and Suryakumar gone
slides.body: In overs 1.5, 3.2 and 5.3, India lost Rahul, Rohit and Suryakumar in quick succession. Each wicket cut India’s win chance by 10-15%, and the bowlers have the momentum now.

slides.headline: India struggled for 4 balls in a row with no runs
slides.body: Between 1.4 and 2.1, the bowlers held India scoreless for 4 balls. That stifling spell made it harder to build momentum, especially after a few good balls earlier.

slides.headline: What to watch from now on – India needs 60 runs in 30 balls
slides.body: With 15 overs done, India must chase 60 runs in the remaining 30 balls – a required run rate of 12. Fast wickets are a threat, so they’ll need big hits and smart shot‑selection to stay alive.

slides.headline: Early wicket trims India's chase, like a safety car on lap one
slides.body: Naseem Shah bowled Rahul (event 0149) in the 2nd over, dropping India's win chance from 46% to 32%. The early loss is like an early safety‑car period that forces the driver to rethink pace.

slides.headline: Over 12 explosion: 20 runs in a single over, tyre wear spikes
slides.body: In the 12th over Mohammad Nawaz unleashed 20 runs – 3.13 σ above the norm. It’s the equivalent of a driver hitting a perfect slipstream and gaining massive speed on a straight.

slides.headline: Mid‑innings collapse: three wickets in three overs cut win chance
slides.body: Rauf’s dismissals (events 0158 and 0171) took the win probability from 30% to 19% then to 15%, mirroring a sudden loss of grip that forces a pit‑stop in the chase’s critical phase.

slides.headline: What to watch: 54 runs needed off 24 balls, chase at 13.5 RRR
slides.body: India now needs 54 runs from 24 balls (13.5 RRR). Think of the final 24 laps at full throttle – Pandya and Kohli’s 75‑run partnership is the current fuel load. Every big hit is a tyre‑change strategy for the win.

slides.headline: Early wicket shakes India's chase
slides.body: Just after the start, Naseem Shah bowled Rahul for a duck at 1.5 overs, dropping India's win chance from 46% to 32%.

slides.headline: Explosive overs boost the total
slides.body: Overs 12 and 18 were fireworks – 20 runs in over 12 and 17 runs in over 18, both far above average, pushing India close to the target.

slides.headline: Pandya‑Kohli partnership steadies the innings
slides.body: Hardik Pandya (38 off 33) and Virat Kohli (61 off 47) built a 98‑run stand, keeping India in the hunt despite early wickets.

slides.headline: What to watch now: 31 runs needed from 12 balls
slides.body: India needs 31 runs off the last 12 balls with a required run rate of 15.5. Keep an eye on the death bowlers – Rauf and Shaheen – and any big hits from the top order.

slides.headline: India's top order is in trouble: 31/3 after 6 overs
slides.body: India are chasing 160 and are already in trouble. Three batters are gone and the score is just 31. Every top-order arrival has been dismissed, leaving them in a tight spot early on.

slides.headline: Haris Rauf is having a nightmare
slides.body: Pakistan's fast bowler Haris Rauf has taken 2 wickets in just 2 overs while conceding 16 runs. He dismissed both Rohit Sharma and Suryakumar Yadav. His pace and bounce are clearly unsettling the Indian batters.

slides.headline: Kohli is still at the crease, but quiet
slides.body: Virat Kohli and Axar Patel are currently batting together. Kohli has 5 off 9 balls, Axar has 2 off 2. They need to build a big partnership right now to breathe some life into this chase.

slides.headline: India need a rocket: 129 from 84 balls
slides.body: To win, India need 129 runs from just 84 more balls — that's nearly 10 runs every over, more than double their current pace. Watch whether Kohli can accelerate or if Pakistan's pace keeps bowling him out.

slides.headline: Hardik’s wides lift India's win chance
slides.body: In the 15th over, Rauf bowled three wides to Hardik Pandya (event 15.5). Those extra deliveries pushed India's win probability from 12% to 16%, a small but vital boost in a tight chase.

slides.headline: Kohli fires back‑to‑back fours
slides.body: At the start of the 17th over Shaheen Shah Afridi gave Kohli a four (17.3) and repeated it on the last ball (17.6). Each shot lifted India's win chance by about 4%, keeping the chase alive.

slides.headline: Only one ball went for nothing
slides.body: The longest spell without a run was just a single dot ball in the 15th over (ball 15.1). It’s a rare blip in an otherwise scoring‑friendly phase.

slides.headline: 31 runs needed from 12 balls – can India finish?
slides.body: India sits at 129/4, needing 31 runs off the final 12 balls with a required run rate of 15.5. Keep an eye on Hardik and Kohli’s strike rotation and any wickets that could swing momentum.

slides.headline: 18th over explodes: 17 runs from Afridi
slides.body: In the 18th over, Shaheen Shah Afridi bowls ten balls, India scoops 17 runs – a sudden burst that lifts the required run rate. It's like a sudden pit stop change in F1, shifting the race pace dramatically.

slides.headline: 16.3: Naseem's dot ball swings the odds
slides.body: On ball 16.3, Naseem Shah bowls a dot to Kohli, reducing India's win chance from 12% to 9%. A single missed run is like a tiny slip in the gearbox – it changes the momentum and raises the required run rate.

slides.headline: Only 12 balls left – 31 runs needed, 15.5 r/r
slides.body: With 12 balls remaining, India needs 31 runs, a required run rate of 15.5. Current run rate is 7.17. It's a sprint: look for big hits, especially from Kohli and Pandya, to close the gap before the final lap.
